court: U.S. District Court, Southern District of Florida; affirmed / vacated by 11th Circuit Court of Appeals
claim_type: Grocery store website inaccessible to blind screen reader users; no accessible online pharmacy refills or store-locator
outcome: District court injunction in favor of plaintiff (2017); 11th Circuit reversed on grounds website is not 'place of public accommodation' but then vacated its own ruling as moot (2021). Case dismissed. Plaintiff did not prevail at appeal level.
estimated_defense_cost: Multi-year appellate litigation; exact figure not disclosed

sources.name: Seyfarth Shaw — 11th Circuit Rules on Winn-Dixie
Southeast ADA Center — Gil v. Winn-Dixie (2021)
National Law Review — 11th Circuit issues highly-anticipated decision
Ogletree — 11th Circuit holds websites not places of public accommodation

summary_one_line: First ADA website accessibility trial in U.S. history (2017); district court ruled for plaintiff but 11th Circuit reversed — illustrates the circuit split and why jurisdiction matters enormously.
notes: District court 2017 injunction required WCAG 2.0 AA conformance within 12 months, ADA web policy, and employee training. 11th Circuit 2021 reversal rejected 'nexus' standard; then vacated its own opinion as moot when the injunction expired. The 9th Circuit (Domino's) and 11th Circuit (Winn-Dixie) represent opposite ends of the circuit split — defendants in the 9th Circuit have far greater exposure.
